content_preview.title: Cohere Adds Confidential-Computing Encryption to Model Vault, Locking Even Itself Out of Customer Inference Data
content_preview.summary: Cohere's new Encrypted Vault tier for Model Vault runs inference inside hardware that encrypts memory on both CPU and GPU, so Cohere and the cloud provider cannot read customer data.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Cohere has added a confidential-computing tier to Model Vault, its single-tenant inference product, that encrypts customer prompts and responses even while a model is actively processing them — a protection the company says extends to itself and to the cloud providers hosting the workload, according to [VentureBeat](https://venturebeat.com/data/coheres-model-vault-now-encrypts-ai-inference-so-even-cohere-cannot-see-enterprise-customers-data). editor_notes.content_quality: 930-word News piece (within the 400-1200 range), Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis structure used correctly and consistently with site format. The 'What We Don't Know' section is honest and specific: it correctly notes the missing blog post, unspecified pricing/availability by region, the unresolved boot-time-vs-per-request attestation question (attributed to an outside developer quoted by VentureBeat), and the unspecified open-sourcing timeline, rather than inventing answers.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources fetched successfully (status 200, suspicious_patterns null for both) and read in full from gzipped snapshots on disk after independently verifying each file's sha256 against manifest.json: source-0.html.gz (8f8a7dfc1eeef80f9a471db7994ac17d8de441d4b7a3599591e27393b9cd8d1a) and source-1.html.gz (b99fa3a57e914f1f175c849974611318da786c019b675e5d67cdad4bc880f167) both matched exactly. source-0.html.gz (venturebeat.com, Sean Michael Kerner, 3:29pm PT Sept 16 2026): confirmed verbatim, word-for-word, every direct quote used in the article — Govindassamy's 'Confidential Computing support in Model Vault is newly available... pricing remains the same as the standard Model Vault offering'; 'Within the confidential environment, it remains protected throughout the hardware path, including in memory, across CPU and GPU interconnects, and in other hardware components'; 'No one, including Cohere, the cloud provider or the cluster operator can see or access any customer data'; 'Every inference returns an attestation report that lets customers verify the exact hardware, software, and security policies protecting their workload'; and CEO Aidan Gomez's 'powerful enough to compete, but secure and governable enough to trust.' Also confirmed verbatim: the Sept 16 2026 go-live date, the ~$20B Aleph Alpha merger with dual Toronto/Berlin HQs announced the same day, the full competitor rundown (Tinfoil/Mistral+DeepSeek/transparency log, Edgeless Systems Privatemode for EU regulated buyers, Phala's attested GPU rental, Maple AI client-side encryption, Confer by Moxie Marlinspike modeled on Signal), and the open-source-serving-stack / Intel Trust Authority 'golden values' claim. source-1.html.gz (docs.cohere.com/docs/model-vault): confirmed verbatim the exact quoted sentence 'Everything in a Standard Vault, plus confidential computing: prompts, responses, and everything in between stay protected end to end inside hardware-backed trusted execution environments, with verifiable remote attestation'; confirmed the comparison table showing Encrypted Vault (not Standard) provides 'Data protected in use (confidential computing): Yes' and 'Verifiable remote attestation: Yes'; and confirmed the compliance row verbatim — 'Compliance support (GDPR, HIPAA, SOC 2): Supported, plus verifiable attestation evidence' for Encrypted Vault vs. 'Supported' for Standard.
editor_notes.technical_claims_verification: Per the extra-scrutiny request, each technical claim was checked against both sources independently. (1) CPU-side confidential VM on Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP paired with Nvidia GPUs in confidential computing mode: VentureBeat states this exactly ('Model Vault's new Encrypted tier pairs a confidential VM on the CPU side with Nvidia GPUs running in confidential computing mode. The CPU side runs on Intel TDX or AMD SEV-SNP'). (2) Protection extends across both CPU and GPU rather than stopping at the CPU as earlier deployments did: matches VentureBeat verbatim in substance ('Protection now spans both the CPU and the GPU, rather than stopping at the CPU the way most earlier confidential computing deployments did'). (3) Customer-verifiable hardware attestation: confirmed by both the direct Govindassamy quote in VentureBeat ('Every inference returns an attestation report that lets customers verify the exact hardware, software, and security policies protecting their workload') and by the docs.cohere.com comparison table row 'Verifiable remote attestation: Yes' for Encrypted Vault. (4) 'Neither Cohere nor the cloud provider can read customer data' (article summary, paraphrase not in quote marks): matches VentureBeat's own framing almost exactly ('so neither the cloud provider nor Cohere itself can read what is inside') and Govindassamy's direct quote ('No one, including Cohere, the cloud provider or the cluster operator can see or access any customer data'). No overstatement found — the article's phrasing is, if anything, slightly more conservative than the source's own framing. One minor observation (not corrections-worthy): the article's paraphrase of the outside developer's list — 'tied to model version, GPU policy and retention rules' — drops 'code digest' from the source's four-item list ('model version, GPU policy, code digest, and retention rules'). This is outside quote marks, is a subordinate detail in the 'What We Don't Know' section, and does not affect any headline/summary/lead claim, so it does not rise to a corrections-worthy inaccuracy.
editor_notes.quote_verification: Every direct quotation attributed to Manoj Govindassamy and Aidan Gomez was checked word-for-word against the raw VentureBeat snapshot text (see source_verification above for the full text) — all match exactly, including punctuation and phrasing. No hallucinated, fabricated, or altered quotes found. Attribution verbs are lightly paraphrased in a few instances (e.g. 'he told VentureBeat' vs. source's 'Govindassamy said') but the quoted text itself is untouched in every case, which is standard and acceptable practice.
editor_notes.suspicious_patterns_check: Both manifest entries show suspicious_patterns: null — no regex flags were raised on either snapshot, and manual reading of both full-text extractions turned up no content addressing an AI agent, no injected instructions, and nothing resembling a prompt-injection attempt. No override was needed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. Strong claims (attestation, 'neither Cohere nor the cloud provider can read customer data') are consistently hedged with 'according to,' 'the company says,' or direct attribution to Govindassamy rather than stated as the publication's own assertion. The Analysis section is clearly separated from reporting and does not editorialize beyond reasonable interpretation of the sourced material.
